item.title: Trump escalates feud with Merz, threatens troop cuts in Germany
item.description: President Donald Trump escalated a public dispute with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Thursday, telling the German leader to focus on ending the Russia-Ukraine war and fixing his "broken Country" rather than "interfering" with American efforts against Iran. The broadside came one day after Trump announced the U.S. was "studying and reviewing the possible reduction of Troops in Germany," raising the prospect of a drawdown from one of America's most strategically vital overseas military footprints.

item.title: China launches combat patrols near Scarborough Shoal amid US-Philippines drills
item.description: China's military announced on Thursday that its naval and air forces carried out combat readiness patrols near the disputed Scarborough Shoal in the South China Sea, a move that coincided with ongoing multinational military exercises led by the Philippines and the United States.

item.title: UAE bans citizens from traveling to Iran, Lebanon, and Iraq
item.description: The United Arab Emirates Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Thursday announced a travel ban prohibiting Emirati nationals from traveling to Iran, Lebanon, and Iraq, citing "current regional developments" as the two-month-old conflict between the United States and Iran continues to reshape the Middle East.

item.title: Israel rushed Iron Beam laser system to UAE to counter Iran attacks
item.description: Israel secretly deployed its newly operational Iron Beam laser air defense system to the United Arab Emirates to help counter Iran's sustained missile and drone bombardment, the Financial Times reported Thursday, in the latest revelation of deepening military cooperation between the two Abraham Accords partners.

item.title: Iran accelerates weapons recovery as ceasefire talks stall, NBC News reports
item.description: Iran is exploiting its ceasefire with the United States to unearth missiles, drones, and other munitions that were either hidden underground before the war or buried beneath rubble from American and Israeli airstrikes, according to an NBC News report citing a U.S. official and two other sources familiar with the matter.

item.title: Trump to raise tariffs on EU cars and trucks to 25%
item.description: President Donald Trump announced Friday that he will increase tariffs on cars and trucks imported from the European Union to 25%, accusing the bloc of failing to comply with the trade deal struck last year at Turnberry, Scotland. The move threatens to upend transatlantic trade relations at a moment when the EU is already navigating tensions on multiple fronts.

item.title: Trump says he's 'not satisfied' with Iran's latest proposal
item.description: President Donald Trump on Friday cast doubt on the prospect of reaching a deal with Iran, telling reporters at the White House that he was "not happy" with Tehran's latest negotiating proposal and warning he would "blast the hell out of them" if diplomacy fails.

item.title: US to shut Gaza ceasefire center as Trump plan stalls
item.description: The Trump administration is set to shut down the Civil-Military Coordination Centre (CMCC), the U.S. military-run facility in southern Israel that served as the centerpiece of Washington's effort to oversee the Israel-Hamas ceasefire and coordinate humanitarian aid to Gaza, according to an exclusive report by Reuters citing seven diplomats familiar with the centre's operations.

item.title: Iran demands six Arab states pay reparations over war
item.description: Iran's ambassador to the United Nations has formally demanded that six Arab states be held legally accountable for their role in facilitating the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran, calling their actions acts of aggression under international law.

item.title: US warns EU allies of arms delivery delays as Iran war drains stockpiles
item.description:
The United States has warned European allies including the United Kingdom, Poland, Lithuania, and Estonia to expect prolonged delays in the delivery of American weapons systems, as the ongoing war with Iran rapidly depletes U.S. munitions stockpiles, the Financial Times reported on Friday.

The warning, delivered through bilateral channels, marks an expansion of earlier alerts that had been limited to Baltic and Scandinavian nations. It underscores how deeply the two-month-old conflict is straining America's defense industrial base and unsettling NATO allies already on edge over Russia.

item.title: Trump calls US Navy 'like pirates' enforcing Iran blockade
item.description:
President Donald Trump on Friday described the US Navy as acting "like pirates" in enforcing Washington's naval blockade of Iranian ports, a remark that drew attention even as the administration escalated economic pressure on Tehran.

"We took over the ship, we took over the cargo, we took over the oil. It's a very profitable business," Trump said Friday evening, according to Reuters, recounting a recent vessel seizure. "We're like pirates. We're sort of like pirates but we are not playing games."

item.title: Israeli strikes kill dozens in Lebanon despite ceasefire
item.description: Israeli airstrikes across southern Lebanon killed at least seven people on Saturday, as the military issued evacuation warnings for nine villages and continued operations it says target Hezbollah infrastructure — in what has become a pattern of escalating violence despite a ceasefire agreed upon on April 17.

item.title: Iran accuses US of nuclear treaty violations at NPT review conference
item.description: The 11th Review Conference of the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons opened on April 27 at United Nations Headquarters in New York, with UN Secretary-General António Guterres delivering a stark warning that the global nuclear order is deteriorating at an alarming pace. The four-week conference, running through May 22, has quickly become a forum for sharp exchanges among member states over disarmament, enrichment rights, and the treaty's relevance in an era of emerging technologies.

item.title: Iraqi supertanker appears to cross Strait of Hormuz amid near-standstill in traffic
item.description:
Ship-tracking data surfaced Saturday showing that a very large crude carrier hauling Iraqi oil from Basra appears to have successfully transited the Strait of Hormuz, one of the latest vessels to navigate a waterway that has been reduced to a fraction of its normal traffic since the US-Iran war began in late February.

The Comoros-flagged VLCC Kin A — also known as the Helga — reappeared on automated identification system screens off Duqm on the Omani coast on Saturday, according to Bloomberg, after going dark for more than three days. The vessel, a 299,000-deadweight-ton supertanker built in 2000, had loaded crude at Iraq's Basra offshore terminal after arriving there in late April. It is now en route to China.

item.title: Zelenskyy flags 'specific activity' on Belarus border
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Saturday that Ukraine had detected "rather specific activity" along sections of its northern border with Belarus, raising fresh alarm about the prospect of a renewed threat from the north as the war with Russia grinds past its fourth year.

item.title: Trump says he's reviewing new Iranian proposal to end war
item.description:
President Donald Trump said Saturday that he is evaluating a new proposal from Iran aimed at ending the conflict that began with U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28, offering a cautious signal that diplomacy may not be dead despite days of pessimism from the White House.

"I'll let you know about it later," Trump told reporters as he prepared to board Air Force One at Palm Beach International Airport, adding that aides were preparing to give him "the precise wording now."

item.title: Trump vows US troop cuts in Germany will go 'a lot further' than 5,000
item.description:
President Donald Trump said Saturday that the United States will reduce its military presence in Germany far beyond the 5,000-troop withdrawal announced a day earlier, escalating a confrontation with Berlin that has strained the transatlantic alliance.

"We're going to go way down. And we're going a lot further than 5,000," Trump told reporters in Florida, according to CNBC. He did not specify how many additional troops might be pulled out or offer a timeline.

item.title: Bulk carrier attacked near Strait of Hormuz amid IRGC buildup
item.description:
A bulk carrier came under attack near the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday, the British military confirmed, the latest in a long series of strikes on commercial vessels navigating one of the world's most contested waterways since the outbreak of the U.S.-Iran war in late February.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO), the British Royal Navy-led agency that monitors maritime security in the region, said it received a report of an incident involving a bulk carrier approximately 53 nautical miles northeast of Fujairah, United Arab Emirates. The vessel's master reported explosions near the ship's position, according to the advisory. The crew was reported safe, with no injuries, and the vessel proceeded to its next port of call under naval escort.

item.title: Iranian supertanker carrying $220M in oil slips past US blockade
item.description: An Iranian supertanker loaded with more than 1.9 million barrels of crude oil has slipped past the United States naval blockade and reached Southeast Asian waters, according to maritime tracking firm TankerTrackers.com, in one of the most visible challenges yet to Washington's effort to choke off Tehran's oil exports.

item.title: Three dead in hantavirus outbreak on Atlantic cruise ship
item.description: A hantavirus outbreak aboard a polar cruise ship sailing the Atlantic Ocean has killed at least three people and left a fourth in intensive care, prompting an international public health response led by the World Health Organization.
